definitions.gloss: owner; master; the person a thing belongs to
definitions.explanation: The person who owns or is responsible for something. On its own it is somewhat old-fashioned, but it is extremely productive as a suffix: {世帯主|せたいぬし} (head of household), {持|も}ち{主|ぬし} (owner), {飼|か}い{主|ぬし} (pet owner), {貸|か}し{主|ぬし} (lender).

examples.japanese: この{財布|さいふ}の{主|ぬし}を{探|さが}している。
examples.english: I'm looking for the owner of this wallet.

examples.japanese: {住民票|じゅうみんひょう}には{世帯主|せたいぬし}の{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}く。
examples.english: You write the head of household's name on the residence certificate.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}の{飼|か}い{主|ぬし}には{散歩中|さんぽちゅう}のマナーが{求|もと}められる。
examples.english: Dog owners are expected to have good manners while walking their dogs.

examples.japanese: この{土地|とち}の{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}が{分|わ}からず、{工事|こうじ}が{進|すす}められないままだ。
examples.english: The owner of this land is unknown, so the construction work still can't move forward.

notes:
The same kanji read あるじ means the master of a house or shop; ぬし is the reading used in compounds about ownership.

COMPOUNDS:
- {世帯主|せたいぬし}: head of household (the official term on forms)
- {持|も}ち{主|ぬし}: owner (of an object, land, or vehicle)
- {飼|か}い{主|ぬし}: owner of a pet
- {地主|じぬし}: landowner, landlord
- {落|お}とし{主|ぬし}: the person who dropped something

USAGE:
Standalone {主|ぬし} sounds literary or archaic today; in modern speech people say {持|も}ち{主|ぬし} or オーナー instead. In folklore, the {主|ぬし} of a lake or forest is its guardian spirit — a large old animal said to rule the place.
